title: The Perception of Visual Surfaces
research_question: To investigate whether the impression of slant of a visual surface is determined by the gradient of texture-density in the retinal image, in isolation from other depth cues.

participants.description: 10 paid Os (9 women, 1 man) for the main experiment, including 3 students, 3 clerical workers, 3 psychology teachers, and 1 engineer. A preliminary experiment used 32 different Os.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Projected lantern-slides of wallpaper patterns (one regular texture with rectangular elements, one irregular texture with unfamiliar elements) photographed at physical slants of 10°, 22°, 30°, and 45° from the perpendicular. Each texture/slant combination was presented with an upward and a downward gradient of texture-density, resulting in 16 standard stimuli. These images were projected onto a translucent screen and viewed monocularly through two hole-screens to eliminate contours, binocular disparity, motion parallax, and differential blur.

measures.instrument: Reproduction task using a 6-inch square composition-board, adjustable by the observer's right hand, rotated 90° backward or forward from a vertical plane. Slants were recorded to the nearest degree.

findings.antecedent: Retinal gradient of texture-density (regular texture, upward increase)
findings.mechanism: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
findings.quote: The positive slopes of the lines joining the means actually obtained show that an increase in 'equivalent physical slant' is accompanied by an increase in the judged slant.

findings.antecedent: Retinal gradient of texture-density (regular texture, downward increase)
findings.mechanism: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
findings.quote: The positive slopes of the lines joining the means actually obtained show that an increase in 'equivalent physical slant' is accompanied by an increase in the judged slant.

findings.antecedent: Retinal gradient of texture-density (irregular texture, upward increase)
findings.mechanism: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
findings.quote: The positive slopes of the lines joining the means actually obtained show that an increase in 'equivalent physical slant' is accompanied by an increase in the judged slant.

findings.antecedent: Retinal gradient of texture-density (irregular texture, downward increase)
findings.mechanism: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
findings.quote: The positive slopes of the lines joining the means actually obtained show that an increase in 'equivalent physical slant' is accompanied by an increase in the judged slant.

findings.consequent: Differential sensitivity to slant (clarity of impression, consistency of judgments)
findings.mechanism: Possibly a regular texture affords a more definite gradient of density than does an irregular texture.
findings.quote: Apparently the regular texture yields a more definite impression of slant.

findings.mechanism: Conflicting cues (e.g., visibility of projection-screen texture, absence of differential blur, lack of accommodation cue, tendency to conform to hole-screen slant, residual head-motion) favored the perception of a frontal surface, leading to a compromise judgment.
findings.quote: The discrepancy between the judged slant and the 'physical slant equivalent to the gradient' is consistently in the direction of a frontal surface.

findings.mechanism: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
findings.quote: As the gradient of density of the texture of a projected image is increased by the experimenter, the slant of the surface perceived increases correspondingly.

findings.antecedent: Experimental setup differences (e.g., more visible screen texture, farther hole-screen, pre-set board)
findings.consequent: Slope of the relationship between texture gradient and judged slant
findings.mechanism: Differences in the experimental setup (e.g., more visible projection screen texture, farther hole-screen, pre-set adjustable board) likely introduced more conflicting cues or strengthened the frontal tendency, leading to weaker perceived slant effects.
findings.quote: There is evidence that the lesser slopes in this experiment are attributable to differences between the two set-ups.

mechanisms: The geometry of perspective dictates that a physical surface not perpendicular to the line of sight projects a distribution of texture-elements which gets denser as the surface recedes, and whose gradient of density is proportional to the angle of slant.
The retinal image is a geometrical inversion of the visual field, which is defined as a projection of the environment on a 'picture-plane.'

The perspective of texture, as distinguished from the perspective of rectilinear outlines, seems to be a fundamental basis for the impression of a three-dimensional environment, or what has been called space.
moderators: Experimental setup differences (e.g., visibility of projection screen texture, distance of hole-screen, pre-setting of adjustable board)
implementation_implications: The perspective of texture seems to be a fundamental basis for the impression of a three-dimensional environment, suggesting that controlling texture gradients in designed environments could influence perceived depth and spatial properties.
Understanding the visual correlates of surface properties like slant can inform design to achieve specific spatial perceptions.

tables.description: Judged Slant as a Function of the Gradient of Texture Density Recorded in Degrees of Tactual-Kinesthetic Inclination to the Vertical. Means of judgments by 10 Os and medians of their standard deviations.

limitations: The translucent plexiglass projection screen had its own texture, which had a contradictory gradient to that of the projected image, potentially affecting results.

The absence of differential blur in the projected image (all parts equally in focus on the frontal screen) contradicted the texture-density gradient and favored the perception of a zero slant (frontal) for the screen itself.
Other factors contributing to a 'frontal tendency' included the tendency for perception to conform to the slant of the hole-screen and any residual head-motion not eliminated by the headrest.

Some observers reported deliberately using cues like size of elements, density of elements, or linear perspective in making judgments, raising questions about the role of inferences versus immediate impressions in the main experiment.
The amount of increase in apparent slant for successively steeper gradients differed markedly between regular and irregular textures, suggesting limitations in generalizability across texture types.

control_conditions: variations in texture gradient properties (e.g., density, size)

mechanism_chain.description: The visual system processes two-dimensional retinal projections of textured surfaces, extracting gradients in texture element properties (like density or size). These gradients are then interpreted to infer the three-dimensional orientation (slant and tilt) of the surface in space.

steps.to_construct: Visual system extracts gradient information (e.g., changes in element size, density)

instruments_used.name: Slant adjustment task
instruments_used.description: Participants adjusted a visual probe (e.g., a line or plane) to match the perceived orientation of the presented surface.
